newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Foot-and-mouth outbreak hits Taiwan pork industry.
newsitem.headline: Foot-and-mouth outbreak hits Taiwan pork industry.

text.p: Taiwan on Thursday banned all pork exports following an outbreak of the highly contagious foot and mouth disease in its hog population, spelling huge losses for one of the island's top export industries.

The cabinet's Council of Agriculture, which said laboratory results confirmed an outbreak of foot and mouth in nine counties and ordered the temporary export ban, warned that Taiwan faced a daunting task in eradicating the deadly disease.

Wholesale pork prices plummeted by as much as 61 percent after the announcement and Taiwan's main consumer watchdog group urged the public to avoid buying pork products that had not been certified as safe by the government.
Because of a holiday in Japan, exporters were waiting until Friday to learn whether the island's single biggest export market would ban imports of Taiwan pork.
The council estimated that Taiwan exported six million out of the 14 million hogs it bred each year -- with 69 percent of all exports going to Japan.
The crisis could deal a heavy blow to Taiwan's economy, where a chronically sluggish recovery had only recently begun to pick up.
According to an industry survey, the hog industry's 1994 net value was T$89 billion ($3.24 billion), representing 20 percent of Taiwan's farm market and 60 percent of the livestock sector.
The Council said instances of the disease had been found in nine counties and more than 20 breeding farms.
"This is an airborne virus that has a very high tolerance to sanitation measures," a council official said.
Worse yet, experts said Taiwan has only 40,000 doses of foot and mouth vaccine, far too little to curb the outbreak.
"There are simply not enough vaccines to go around," a council official said.
The council said it would import more vaccines immediately.
Japan, Taiwan's largest pork export market, has not been infected by the disease and was expected to impose its own ban on pork shipments from Taiwan, experts said.

Japan had been importing some 16,000 tonnes of fresh and frozen pork from Taiwan per month, despite Tokyo's imposition of a special "emergency" import tariff to limit imports and protect local breeders.
South Korea was another major destination.
Japan imported about 183,494 tonnes of pork from Taiwan in 1995, ranking Taiwan its largest supplier.
Exporters fear a Japanese ban would simply hand the market to competitors in the United States, Canada and Europe.
Taiwan's pork exports had been limited mainly to Japan because both were battling hog cholera, another contagious disease that has seen scattered outbreaks in Taiwan's huge stockyards for years.
Japan has launched a campaign to eliminate hog cholera by 1999, forcing Taiwan to consider a similar programme for fear of losing its main export market.
Japan has said it would ban imports from cholera-infected areas once it gained control over the disease.
Analysts said the crisis would hurt many pork-related downstream businesses, particularly the feed industry.
Grain importers said the ban could result in a decline of about 120 million tonnes of feed corn a year, or one-fifth of Taiwan's total corn imports.
